fixes.explanation: Close, friend, because Pharaoh's palace has plenty of officers. Genesis 40:2 mentions Pharaoh's chief cupbearer, but that title isn't Potiphar's. Genesis 39:1 says he's captain of the guard. A guard captain carrying a tray of cups would confuse everybody at the door.

Army is a fair guess for a captain of the guard, friend. But verse 4 says Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his household and entrusted him with everything he owned. Joseph isn't marching anybody anywhere. He's running the house. If somebody handed me an army, I'd have every soldier stamped with a cookie pattern by lunch.

Verse 6 says Potiphar “…did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate.” Joseph had all he owned in his care, and the only thing left on Potiphar's mind was his meal. Friend, if the only thing on my mind were cookies, I'd need a bigger apron.

A free man would be a happy ending, friend, but we're not there yet. Verse 22 says the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph's care, so Joseph is still inside. Promoted, yes, but that door is still locked. And verse 23 tells us why the warden could relax: the LORD was with Joseph.
